patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Nextiva documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.

General-purpose vs specialist. Choose Nextiva only if your buying job matches “SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo” rather than Slack's shape. Choose Slack only if your buying job matches “Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $1” rather than Nextiva's shape. Workflow advantage: Nextiva leans business-phone, customer-messaging; Slack leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Nextiva documents a broader use-case set; Slack is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Nextiva is SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month annual, with messaging apps including WhatsApp; Slack is Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Business+ $15, Enterprise+ contact sales; huddles for light vi.
- Workflow coverage skew: Nextiva-leaning business-phone, customer-messaging, contact-center vs Slack-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Nextiva — Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Slack — Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer.

Limitations — Nextiva: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Analytics and AI assistance require Scale / higher plans or XBert add-on from $99/mo; Slack: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer; No SMS or WhatsApp Business customer channels.

Poor-fit cases: Nextiva is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included · Slack is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone system — no cloud phone, call routing, recording or power dialer · Avoid Nextiva if you actually need Slack's motion (Channel-based team messaging platform — Free $0, Pro $7.25/user/month annual, Bu)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
